messages.body_plain:
Hi Asuman,

You cannot compare between different contexts for the same sample, as they are distinct exclusive Cytosine positions in the genome and you will never be able to merge (unite) them. For detecting differential methylation you need to compare two distinct samples, but the context must be the same.

Best,
Alex

It can also happen when you try to convert a methylKit DB object into a methylKit object (saved in the RAM) and then try to subset the object with the function "regionCounts"  using a bed file. Although no error is diplayed when putting the methylKit object in the RAM, the error will happen afterwards when doing the subsetting. This is because the object in RAM is incomplete with many lines containing NAs (try checking the end of your R object with tail()). This causes a bug with the IRanges overlapping tool. The solution is to provide more RAM to the code execution. I solved the bug when running in local instead of using the server but did not understand at first why it was not working in one case.

I am using MethylKit to understand the methylation signature in my samples that are derived from cell-free DNA. In my methylation analysis, I ran only the CpG from the overall CX report that bismark generates. I ran this piece of code to understand the std. deviation of the covered CpG
library(methylKit)

                 'ALS3_793_hg19/ALS3_CG_report.txt',
                 'ALS4_794_hg19/ALS4_CG_report.txt',
                 'ALS6_798_hg19/ALS6_CG_report.txt',
                 'ALS7_797_hg19/ALS7_CG_report.txt',
                 'ALS8_799_hg19/ALS8_CG_report.txt',
                 'ACRI22_795_hg19/ACRI22_CG_report.txt',
                 'ACRI247_796_hg19/ACRI247_CG_report.txt',
                 'Prost018_791_hg19/Prost018_CG_report.txt'
)

myobj2 = methRead(location = file.list, sample.id <http://sample.id> = list("ALS1","ALS3","ALS4","ALS6", "ALS7", "ALS8", "ACRI22", "ACRI247", "Prost018"),
                  assembly = "hg19", dbtype = "tabix", pipeline = "bismarkCytosineReport",
                  header = FALSE, skip = 0, sep = "\t", resolution = "base",
                  treatment = c(1,1,1,1,1,1,0,0,0), dbdir = "ALS_methyl_call", mincov = 5)
meth=methylKit::unite(myobj2)
pm=percMethylation(meth)
mds=matrixStats::rowSds(pm)
hist(mds,col="cornflowerblue",xlab="Std. dev. per CpG")
the graph I got is this:

then I changed my min.cov value to 10 and also added min.per.group=1L and then again made std.dev.histo:

#this will add those rows in my object, in which from at least one sample, there are Cs/Ts with coverage of 10
meth.min=unite(myobj,min.per.group=1L)

I expected the second histogram should have had more frequency as I took into account those CpG calls where I get at least one sample having Cs/Ts with minCov10? Please correct me if I am wrong. The obtained numbers of sites are calculated from the unique number of genes names in the "distance from TSS" file.

I hope my question made a little sense. I wanted to understand why the ultimate number of CpGs is more despite the fact that frequency in the second histogram is less.

I would appreciate your help.

Shruti
